name: VVIX/VIX ratio stress precursor
thesis: Vol-of-vol rich vs vol (VVIX/VIX ratio z) marks fragile hedging complexes that precede equity drawdowns
mechanism: When VVIX is elevated relative to VIX, convexity demand exceeds spot-vol demand; this imbalance signals dealer stress and tail-risk accumulation in the hedging complex.
orthogonality_note: Ratio of higher-order vol to spot vol is mechanistically distinct from spot VIX level or SKEW; captures vol-of-vol premium not SKEW tail insurance.
evidence_note: VVIX as a predictor of equity vol regimes: Park (2015), Johnson (2017); vol-of-vol premium studied in Huang & Shaliastovich (2014).

name: CBOE SKEW percentile tail-demand
thesis: Elevated SKEW percentile = tail-hedge demand; test whether it carries any forward drawdown information (literature says weak — a clean null is content)
mechanism: High SKEW signals elevated OTM put premium relative to ATM; tail-demand could front-run dealer de-risking or mark crowded hedging that dampens actual drawdowns (contrarian interpretation).
orthogonality_note: SKEW measures OTM put vs call skewness; orthogonal to VIX (spot vol level) and VVIX/VIX ratio; different signal family.
evidence_note: Vilkov & Xiao (2012); Chang, Christoffersen & Jacobs (2013); literature consistently finds weak predictive power — null hypothesis well-documented.

name: VIX term-structure slope
thesis: Backwardation (front>back) percentile as stress state vs contango carry-calm; slope z vs forward SPY excess return
mechanism: VIX futures backwardation signals near-term risk elevation exceeds forward risk; historically associated with mean-reverting stress events and vol-risk premium compression.
orthogonality_note: VIX term-structure slope captures the futures-curve shape; distinct from spot VIX level, VVIX, and SKEW.
evidence_note: Campasano & Simon (2018); Mixon (2007); term structure slope as stress signal widely studied — limited tracked history in current store.
screen_rejection_reasons: Gate 3 FAIL: sample < 5 years (probed from file span or history_years field)

name: COT ES net-spec positioning extreme
thesis: Extreme speculative net length in ES fades forward; standalone single-series construction testing whether crowded spec-longs predict negative excess returns
mechanism: CFTC legacy spec net-long in ES reflects retail/trend-follower positioning; extremes tend to be crowded and mean-revert. Weekly CFTC data, published Friday; pipeline applies lag n=3 rows on weekly series = ~3-week effective lag (more than covers the 3-day CFTC publication delay; conservative).

data.pit: weekly CFTC Tuesday data, published Friday; pipeline lag n=3 rows on weekly series = ~3-week row-lag (plus run_spec shift(1) = ~4-week effective lag); conservative, no same-week leakage

orthogonality_note: CFTC net-spec positioning measures futures-market participant imbalance; mechanistically distinct from vol, credit spreads, and sentiment surveys.
evidence_note: Wang (2003), Sanders, Irwin & Merrin (2010); COT net-spec as contrarian equity predictor has moderate literature support.

name: COT UST10y spec positioning squeeze
thesis: Crowded short/long spec positioning in 10y futures precedes squeeze reversals in duration
mechanism: Extreme speculative net positioning in 10y T-Note futures tends to mean-revert as crowded trades unwind; squeeze direction predicted by extreme sign. Weekly CFTC data, published Friday; pipeline applies lag n=3 rows on weekly series = ~3-week effective lag (conservative).

data.pit: weekly CFTC Tuesday data, published Friday; pipeline lag n=3 rows on weekly series = ~3-week row-lag (plus run_spec shift(1) = ~4-week effective lag); conservative, no same-week leakage

orthogonality_note: 10y spec positioning is mechanistically distinct from credit spreads and equity sentiment; captures rate-futures crowding not equity dynamics.
evidence_note: Hartzmark & Solomon (2012); Kang, Rouwenhorst & Tang (2014); COT spec extremes in rates documented as squeeze precursors.

name: NAAIM exposure extremes
thesis: Active-manager exposure extremes (very low = capitulation, very high = complacency) vs forward SPY
mechanism: NAAIM survey reflects active manager equity allocation; extremes mark behavioural capitulation (low) or complacency (high), both historically mean-reverting. Weekly Thursday release, 1-week publication lag enforced.

data.pit: weekly survey, published Thursday, 1-week lag enforced in pipeline

orthogonality_note: NAAIM surveys active managers (not retail); distinct from AAII survey, COT positioning, and vol sentiment; measures professional allocation decision.
evidence_note: Brown & Cliff (2004); Baker & Wurgler (2006) sentiment framework; NAAIM-specific: Blitz, Huij & Martens (2011) style exposure reversals.

name: HY OAS widening velocity
thesis: SPEED of high-yield spread widening (21d diff z), distinct from the scored bond-health LEVEL composite, as drawdown-onset precursor
mechanism: Rapid HY spread widening signals tightening financial conditions and credit-risk repricing before equity markets fully adjust; velocity captures regime shift earlier than level.

data.pit: FRED daily, minor revision, pit proxy

orthogonality_note: Velocity of spread change (diff z) is mechanistically distinct from the level composite used in bond-health scores; captures momentum in credit conditions.
evidence_note: Mueller, Vedolin & Zhou (2011); Gilchrist & Zakrajsek (2012); HY spread velocity as leading indicator of equity drawdowns well-documented.

name: Quality-spread momentum (BAA-AAA)
thesis: Momentum in the BAA-AAA quality spread captures credit-quality risk repricing ahead of equities
mechanism: BAA-AAA spread widening signals flight from lower-quality credit; 63d momentum in the spread captures persistent deterioration in credit quality sentiment before equity repricing.
orthogonality_note: Quality spread (BAA-AAA) isolates credit-quality premium distinct from HY OAS (which blends default + liquidity); momentum in quality spread is a different dimension from level.
evidence_note: Estrella & Mishkin (1998); Krishnamurthy & Vissing-Jorgensen (2011); quality spread as macro/credit cycle indicator extensively studied.

name: BTC hashrate momentum
thesis: Hashrate contraction (miner capitulation) then recovery marks accumulation regimes; hashrate 63d momentum z vs forward BTC
mechanism: Declining hashrate signals miner capitulation and selling pressure; recovery signals returning profitability. 63d pct-change z captures the sign of the accumulation/distribution cycle.
orthogonality_note: Hashrate momentum is on-chain proof-of-work supply signal; orthogonal to price-derived MVRV valuation gauge, active addresses, and VDD multiple.
evidence_note: Puell Multiple / hashrate-ratio studies (Woo 2019); miner capitulation as BTC cycle marker: Burniske & Tatar (2017).

name: BTC network-activity impulse
thesis: Active-address growth impulse leads price in adoption waves; distinct series from the confirmer MVRV/Reserve-Risk valuation gauge
mechanism: Accelerating active addresses signal new-user adoption or network congestion driving demand; 63d pct-change in active addresses captures the impulse of demand growth before price fully adjusts.
orthogonality_note: Active-address growth impulse (demand-side) is mechanistically distinct from hashrate momentum (supply-side), VDD multiple (value-days-destroyed), and MVRV valuation.
evidence_note: Metcalfe's Law in BTC: Peterson (2018); Alabi (2017); on-chain active address growth as leading adoption metric.

name: Equity put/call ratio extreme
thesis: Extreme put/call readings mark sentiment washouts/complacency; contrarian vs forward SPY
mechanism: High equity put/call ratio marks fear/hedging extremes that historically precede relief rallies; low ratio marks complacency preceding drawdowns.
orthogonality_note: Equity put/call ratio captures retail options-market sentiment; distinct from NAAIM (professional allocation), COT (futures positioning), and SKEW (OTM premium).
evidence_note: Whaley (2000); Blau, Ness & Ness (2004); equity P/C ratio as sentiment contrarian indicator documented, CBOE history limited in tracked store.

name: BTC VDD-multiple percentile
thesis: Value-days-destroyed multiple percentile flags old-coin distribution; rich percentile precedes deeper BTC drawdowns
mechanism: VDD-multiple high readings indicate long-held coins (high value-days-destroyed) are being spent/distributed, historically a cycle-top signal.
orthogonality_note: VDD-multiple measures coin-age-weighted transfer volume; distinct from active addresses (demand signal), hashrate (supply/miner), and MVRV (valuation).
evidence_note: CheckOnChain VDD multiple: Woo (2020); coin-day-destruction studies Kondor et al. (2014); old-coin spending as cycle-top warning.
